evidence.claim: Global policy assigns outcome ownership, evidence-first routing, bounded delegation, validation, memory, and safety to the PI orchestrator.
README describes Evolvera PI as a shared terminal and VS Code harness whose principal PI remains responsible for the result.
README defines system prompt, agents, skills, extensions, runtime settings, subagents, MCP, project artifacts, and routing responsibilities.
README documents VS Code entry commands and the external bridge capabilities.
README documents versioned checkout deployment into the global runtime and preservation/overwrite behavior.
README documents update, reload, and rollback from versioned checkouts.
Unix installer validates Node, installs PI, copies configuration/agents/skills/extensions/themes, preserves existing MCP config, and installs PI packages.
Windows installer performs the platform-equivalent runtime deployment and package installation.
Runtime settings select provider/model/thinking/theme and declare installed packages.
Subagent package concurrency is configured with maxConcurrent 8.
MCP configuration declares a lazy Context7 server launched through npx.
Project-memory extension reads Markdown summary and normalized architecture JSON, compares Git HEAD, and injects a compact index before agent start.
Subagent watchdog adds lifecycle guards, notifications, stop RPC, and resume policy for planner-heavy.
Agent guide defines delegation tiers, reconciled change-contract gate, self-contained handoffs, and scout/planner/builder roles.
Planner workflow defines evidence intake, reconciled contracts, normalized plan artifacts, scheduling, and execution gates.
Builder workflow defines bounded target ownership, tier routing, checkpoint expectations, validation, and stop rules.
Testing workflow defines SHA-bound post-build evidence, stateful-resource gates, and PASS/BLOCKED/UNVERIFIED verdicts.
Flow defines GitHub-first re-entry, approval gates, issue/DAG delivery, exclusive claims, branch/worktree isolation, review, and closure policy.
Flow defines durable Project plan, schedule, DAG, and index artifacts while excluding dynamic delivery state from memory.
Website pipeline orders strategy, design, optional creativity, content, planning, building, polishing, and validation.
Project-memory skill defines Markdown narrative, normalized JSON, derived HTML, initial scan, validation, rendering, and summary injection.
PI Studio is a local workspace web interface with per-project sessions, JSONL history, streaming RPC, Docker option, and fake-RPC smoke testing.
PI Studio server spawns pi --mode rpc, writes JSON commands to stdin, parses stdout, and broadcasts RPC events over SSE.
PI Studio server exposes bootstrap, project open, events, command, history, and session routes.
Studio browser bootstraps projects, opens a project, subscribes to SSE, sends RPC commands, and submits prompts.
Studio reads per-project JSONL session history from the global agent sessions directory.
PI Studio container installs @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent version 0.80.3.

gaps.title: PI Studio Docker version drift

gaps.title: MCP adapter internals are external
gaps.impact: The map can evidence configuration and package use, but not adapter implementation details.
gaps.question: Which exact lifecycle and transport semantics does the external pi-mcp-adapter package implement?

gaps.title: VS Code bridge source is external
gaps.impact: Only documented entry points and bridge capabilities are represented.
gaps.question: How does the external VS Code extension implement its bridge to the PI runtime?

gaps.title: Live delivery state is intentionally excluded
gaps.impact: Architecture memory describes record types and policy, not current boards, claims, issues, or PR status.
gaps.question: Current delivery state must be read from GitHub during Flow re-entry, not this snapshot.
